header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: Day, let him honour his guest.” The Prophet ﷺ said this three times. A man asked, “O Rasulullah, what is honouring the guest?” Rasulullah ﷺ said, “It is to host the guest for three days; if the guest stays on even after three days, hosting him is a kindness of the host” (not feeding him after three days would not be an act contrary to human nature). Hazrat Abu Sa'id Khudri (RA) narrates this.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ الْمِقْدَامِ اَبِيْ كَرِيْمَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: اَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ اَضَافَ قَوْمًا فَاَصْبَحَ الضَّيْفُ مَحْرُوْمًا فَاِنَّ نَصْرَهُ حَقٌّ عَلَي كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ حَتَّي يَاْخُذَ بِقِرَي لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ زَرْعِهِ وَمَالِهِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب ماجاء في الضيافة رقم:٣٧٥١
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Miqdam Abu Karimah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said: “If anyone comes as a guest to (someone among) a people, and he is not hosted until the next morning (the one who accepted him as a guest did not provide him hospitality that night), then helping him is a duty upon every Muslim. Moreover, he has the right to take from the host's wealth and from his crops as much as the guest needs for a night's meal.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- This is only when the guest has no arrangement at all to eat and drink, and he is in a situation of compulsion. Otherwise, providing hospitality is a duty upon the host on the basis of humanity and decency.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ قَالَ: دَخَلَ عَلَيَّ
